gloss: branding iron; brand mark; burn mark (stamped with a heated iron)

definitions.gloss: branding iron; brand mark; burn mark (stamped with a heated iron)
definitions.explanation: A mark made by pressing a heated metal stamp onto a surface, or the tool used to make such marks.

examples.japanese: どら{焼|や}きに{焼|や}き{印|いん}を{押|お}す。
examples.english: To press a brand mark onto a dorayaki.

examples.japanese: この{木箱|きばこ}には{焼|や}き{印|いん}で{名前|なまえ}が{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: This wooden box has a name branded into it.

examples.japanese: {和菓子屋|わがしや}では{店|みせ}の{名前|なまえ}の{焼|や}き{印|いん}を{使|つか}うことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Japanese confectionery shops often use branding irons with their shop name.

notes:
A compound of {焼|や}く (to burn/grill) and {印|いん} (mark/seal). In Japanese traditional crafts, branding irons are commonly used to mark wooden products, leather goods, and sweets. Japanese confections like {饅頭|まんじゅう} and どら{焼|や}き often bear the shop's brand mark as a decorative element.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{印|いん}を{押|お}す: to brand, to press a mark
- {焼|や}き{印|いん}を{入|い}れる: to put a brand mark on
- {店名|てんめい}の{焼|や}き{印|いん}: brand mark with the shop name

RELATED WORDS:
- {烙印|らくいん}: brand, stigma — can also be used figuratively for a mark of shame
- {刻印|こくいん}: engraving, stamped mark — carved rather than burned
- {印|しるし}: mark, symbol — broader term for any kind of mark
